title: Affine transformation of a Gaussian product measure
statement: Let $I$ be a finite set, let $c=(c_i)_{i\in I}\in\mathbb R^I$, and let $s\in\mathbb R$. The map $y\mapsto(c_i+s y_i)_{i\in I}$ sends the product of standard Gaussian measures on $\mathbb R^I$ to the product of Gaussian measures with means $c_i$ and variances $s^2$.
replaced: Let $I$ be finite, $c\in\mathbb R^I$, and $s\in\mathbb R$. The map $y\mapsto(c_i+sy_i)_i$ pushes $\bigotimes_iN(0,1)$ to $\bigotimes_iN(c_i,s^2)$, including negative or zero $s$.
